Stage 01

Pre-Incorporation & Know-Your-Customer

UBO transparency, Apostille authentication chain, official name clearance restricted wordlist, and pre-incorporation statutory fee budget.

UBO Ultimate Beneficial Owner Screening Rules Public Registry Disclosure

>=25% ownership / control

Applicable AML statute: Law 10/2010 of 28 April on Prevention of Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing, as amended by Law 11/2021 of 9 July implementing EU Directive 2018/843/5AMLD; Royal Decree 304/2014 of 5 May on implementing regulations; Royal Decree 100/2022 of 8 February establishing the Single Beneficial Ownership Register (Registro Único de Titularidades Reales) managed by the General Directorate of Registries and Notaries (DGRN) under the Ministry of Justice; Article 42 of Law 10/2010 and the Corporate Enterprises Act Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010; SEPBLAC (Servicio Ejecutivo de la Comisión de Prevención del Blanqueo de Capitales y Delitos Monetarios) Circular 1/2021.
Registered Agent & Physical Address Licensed Agent Required

A virtual office may be accepted as the provisional registered and tax domicile for a maximum of three months post-incorporation, provided the SL holds an annual lease agreement for at least €6,000 in office sub-services within Spanish territory and at least one director is resident in the European Union. However, for the ISIC 4100 slip-form reinforced concrete silo and aeration tower EPC scope, the AEAT (Spanish Tax Agency) and SEPBLAC require demonstrable commercial substance: a physical or otherwise fully accessible office where contracts, payroll records, construction logs, and corporate books are maintained, and where the operative project-management equipment can be examined. A pure virtual mailbox without such accessibility will be presumptively treated as a shell company (sociedad pantalla) under Article 42 of Law 10/2010 and may trigger immediate company-registry and tax-audit intervention.

Stage 02

Statutory Formation & Board Resolutions

Competent registry, governing statute, capital lockup rules, and first board resolution template.

Competent corporate registry

Registro Mercantil Central for name certification; provincial Registro Mercantil of the registered office for inscription; Spanish notary for execution of the public deed.

Governing statute

Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, por el que se aprueba el texto refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital (LSC), Articles 4, 19-22, 62, 67, 124-129, 210-216; Código de Comercio Articles 119-124.

Formation / constitutional filings

Escritura pública de constitución (public deed of incorporation) electronically transmitted by the notary to the Registro Mercantil and to the Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria.

Incorporation processing time

⚡ 24 business days (SOP sum)

Paid-up Capital & Blocked Account Regime Mandatory Capital Deposit & Lockup

Minimum share capital EUR 3,000 (Art. 4 LSC), fully subscribed and paid-in at subscription; cash contributions must be deposited in an escrow account opened in the notary's name at a Spanish credit institution (Art. 62 LSC) and remain blocked until registration; non-cash contributions require an independent expert valuation report (Art. 67 LSC).

Funding & unlock path: Fire safety certificate per Código Técnico de la Edificación (CTE DB-SI) and Real Decreto 513/2017 (RIPCI); structural load inspection per Código Estructural (Real Decreto 470/2021); workplace health and safety plan per Ley 31/1995 and Real Decreto 1627/1997, including the site-specific Plan de Seguridad y Salud for silo elevation works.

Paid-in capital rule: Minimum share capital EUR 3,000 (Art. 4 LSC), fully subscribed and paid-in at subscription; cash contributions must be deposited in an escrow account opened in the notary's name at a Spanish credit institution (Art. 62 LSC) and remain blocked until registration; non-cash contributions require an independent expert valuation report (Art. 67 LSC).

Pro-Forma First Board Resolution Draft
RESOLVED, that the company is validly constituted under the Ley de Sociedades de Capital and its Bylaws. FIRST: The incorporation deed having been granted and subscribed, the shareholders' contributions of EUR 3,000 are ratified and accepted, constituting the subscribed share capital. SECOND: The company adopts as its registered office the premises stated in the deed and designates its legal representative for tax and administrative purposes. THIRD: Mr./Ms. [Name] is appointed Sole Administrator, with powers per Bylaw Article [X], accepting office now. FOURTH: The Administration is instructed to execute the registration filing in the Registro Mercantil, obtain the NIF, publish incorporation in BORME, and complete municipal licensing. FIFTH: Minutes approved and signed.
Industrial Access / EIA & Civil Defense Approval Mandatory Environmental Clearance

Consejería de Industria of the autonomous community; municipal Ayuntamiento for activity licensing; Registro Oficial de Licitadores y Empresas Clasificadas del Sector Público for construction contractor classification.

Category: Licencia de actividad / Declaración responsable de establecimiento industrial (apertura y funcionamiento) and, where undertaking public works, clasificación empresarial as a construction contractor.

Stage 03

Tax Identity & Indirect Tax

Tax authority e-portal, entity tax classification elections, VAT thresholds, and 0% export documentation chain.

Tax ID Application Infrastructure

Competent tax authority

Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); official portal: sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es

E-government filing portal

For a Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL), the public deed of incorporation must be presented at the relevant Registro Mercantil and, simultaneously, the provisional NIF (Código de Identificación Fiscal) is obtained from AEAT. After full registration of the company, AEAT issues the definitive NIF. For foreign entities without a permanent establishment, a non-resident NIF must be requested through a fiscal representative or by directly filing Form 036, attaching the certificate of incorporation, proof of registered office, and articles of association; the representative must be resident in Spain. The SL, as a resident entity, is subject to the general corporate income tax regime and must complete Form 036/037 for registration in the Census of Entrepreneurs, Professionals and Retainers before commencing activities.

Tax ID type & application path: Entity_Level_Taxation; resident Spanish SLs are subject to Impuesto sobre Sociedades (Corporate Income Tax) at the standard rate of 25% on worldwide income, unless the reduced 15% rate for newly created companies applies. Territorial scope is worldwide for resident entities. No general tax-exempt zone applies to the SL itself. — For a Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL), the public deed of incorporation must be presented at the relevant Registro Mercantil and, simultaneously, the provisional NIF (Código de Identificación Fiscal) is obtained from AEAT. After full registration of the company, AEAT issues the definitive NIF. For foreign entities without a permanent establishment, a non-resident NIF must be requested through a fiscal representative or by directly filing Form 036, attaching the certificate of incorporation, proof of registered office, and articles of association; the representative must be resident in Spain. The SL, as a resident entity, is subject to the general corporate income tax regime and must complete Form 036/037 for registration in the Census of Entrepreneurs, Professionals and Retainers before commencing activities.

Default Tax Classification & Elections

Default tax classification

Entity_Level_Taxation; resident Spanish SLs are subject to Impuesto sobre Sociedades (Corporate Income Tax) at the standard rate of 25% on worldwide income, unless the reduced 15% rate for newly created companies applies. Territorial scope is worldwide for resident entities. No general tax-exempt zone applies to the SL itself.

Available election forms

Spain does not implement a check-the-box system; an SL is a mandatory corporate tax resident and cannot elect pass-through treatment. Available elections include (i) the regulated group consolidation regime for groups (articles 42 et seq. of Law 27/2014), (ii) the optional reduced corporate income tax rate and certain deductions for investment, (iii) the option to apply the Special Tax Regime for ventures (start-ups) under Law 28/2022, and (iv) the applicability of the EU Anti-Tax-Avoidance Directive hybrid mismatch rules, which do not allow elective recharacterization but mandate self-correcting adjustments. VAT group status (régimen especial de grupo de entidades) may be elected under Article 163 quinquies of Law 37/1992 when economic, financial, and organizational links exist.

VAT / GST & 0% Export Zero-Rating

Standard VAT / GST rate

21%

Mandatory registration threshold (Nexus)

No general EUR turnover threshold triggers mandatory IVA registration; every entrepreneur or professional carrying out taxable supplies in Spanish territory must apply for registration before starting activities (Ley 37/1992). For the special simplified regime (régimen simplificado), quantitative limits apply: generally EUR 250,000 per year for most agricultural and construction activities, and EUR 150,000 for certain others; crossing these limits mandates exit from the simplified regime rather than entry into the standard regime.

Export 0% zero-rating conditions

Export of goods to destinations outside the European Union qualifies for 0% VAT under Article 21 of Law 37/1992, provided the exporter is established in Spanish territory and the goods depart from the EU within the legally required period (normally 90 days from dispatch, extendable). The zero rate applies upon proof of physical departure from the EU customs territory, obtained through the Single Administrative Document (DUA). For services relating to real property or goods exported outside the EU, or certain transportation ancillary services, the zero rate applies if the recipient is a non-established taxable person and the effective use and exploitation occurs outside the EU. Services directly connected with goods to be exported may be zero-rated with a retention of evidence of the customs export declaration.

  • Customs Export Declaration (DUA/SAD)
  • Bill of Lading (maritime) or Airway Bill (air) or CMR (road transport)
  • Inward Remittance Certificate or Foreign Currency Credit Advice evidencing the receipt of payment from the foreign buyer

All B2B invoices must be issued electronically and transmitted in an interoperable structured format under the Crea y Crece framework (Law 18/2022), with mandatory implementation for sellers with turnover over EUR 8 million by May 2026 and all others by May 2027. In addition, large enterprises and VAT groups (under the Suministro Inmediato de Información del IVA, SII) must send invoice records to AEAT within four business days of issuance using approved web services or EDI/API. The new Verifactura system requires an electronic invoice with a digital signature or QR code verifying authenticity and integrity, and AEAT will maintain a clearing platform; non-compliant invoices are not considered legally receivable.

AEAT may retrospectively review export zero-rating claims within the four-year limitation period. If the required customs and payment documentation is missing or inconsistent, AEAT will assess the unpaid VAT at 21% on the presumed taxable value, plus default interest, and apply penalties under Article 27 of Law 58/2003 (late payment surcharge) and Article 191 (non-declared tax) ranging from 50% to 150% of the tax omitted. In aggravated tax fraud cases, criminal liability may arise if the amount defrauded exceeds EUR 120,000, with penalties up to six years imprisonment. The clawback also extends to fraudulent claims made through shell structures or unrepatriated foreign currency where the exporter fails to demonstrate the real commercial transaction.

Stage 04

Banking & Treasury Architecture

Central-bank FX diagnosis, tier-1 local banks vs offshore digital EMI matrix, and KYC rejection defense guide.

Foreign Exchange Regime & Central Bank Policy

Current-account convertibility

Spain applies no exchange-control licensing regime; capital and current-account convertibility are fully liberalized under Articles 63-66 TFEU and Law 18/1992, with the euro as legal tender. Profit remittance obstacles are procedural only: obtain the foreign shareholder's NIE, settle the 19% non-resident income-tax withholding (reduced under applicable double-tax treaties), and file the Banco de España Balance-of-Payments statistical declaration for any cross-border payment above €10,000. Law 19/2023 on foreign direct investment additionally requires prior authorization for non-EU/EFTA investments in critical infrastructure, defence, dual-use technology or national-security areas; an ISIC 4100 grain-silo-elevator EPC business is not presumptively within those sectors, provided no site lies near a regulated military or state-security perimeter.

Export proceeds surrender rules

There is no statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement in Spain: no conversion ratio, no deposit timeline and no repatriation quota are imposed by the Banco de España or the Eurosystem. An exporting SL may retain foreign-currency receipts indefinitely in multi-currency accounts and convert at commercial market rates. The sole compliance layer is statistical and fiscal: cross-border transactions exceeding €10,000 must be reported through the Banco de España BOPS electronic declarations, and export gains must be recognized for Corporate Income Tax (IS) purposes at the ECB reference exchange rate on accrual, with supporting SWIFT/LC evidence retained for six years under Law 10/2010 AML rules.

Central bank supervision: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), operating within the Eurosystem and the European Central Bank (ECB) Single Supervisory Mechanism; exchange and capital-movement statistical competence also lies with the Directorate General for International Trade and Investment (Dirección General de Comercio Internacional e Inversiones) of the Spanish Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business.

Offshore Digital Bank / EMI Whitelist

Cross-border EMI / Fintech rails Fit: High

Low-Medium feasibility: only European Economic Area (EEA) Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) validly passported into Spain under Law 21/2011 and PSD2 may lawfully serve as payment-account or e-money processors; they can expedite SEPA concentration and supplier disbursements but are not acceptors of statutory share-capital deposits because Spanish Notaries require a deposit certificate from a credit institution (bank) to authenticate the capital desembolso. Offshore, non-EEA EMIs have no legal mandate in Spain, cannot provide the notarial escrow evidence, and their use as treasury rail exposes the SL to adverse AML classification under Law 10/2010; therefore they should be confined to ancillary collection gateways only after a tier-1 bank account is live.

Core KYC Rejection Triggers & Defense Dossier

Foreign shareholder incorporated in a jurisdiction on FATF grey-listing, Spain's Royal Decree 304/2014 high-risk list, or an EU non-cooperative jurisdiction.

Root cause: Foreign shareholder incorporated in a jurisdiction on FATF grey-listing, Spain's Royal Decree 304/2014 high-risk list, or an EU non-cooperative jurisdiction.

Defense evidence: Certificate of tax residence from the foreign tax authority, audited financial statements for the prior two years, a complete natural-person UBO chain on the official Spanish UBO register form, bank reference letter from the shareholder's credit institution, and a notarized statement of the commercial rationale for owning the Spanish grain-silo EPC vehicle.
Missing NIE for any non-resident director or missing inscription of the SL deed in the Registro Mercantil at onboarding.

Root cause: Missing NIE for any non-resident director or missing inscription of the SL deed in the Registro Mercantil at onboarding.

Defense evidence: NIE certificates for each director and shareholder, certified copy of the escritura de constitución, certificate of registration and incorporation from the Registro Mercantil, plus the appointment deed of an authorized Spanish-resident administrator (with NIE) for service of process and banking operations.
Politically exposed person (PEP) status of an ultimate shareholder, or layered offshore holding creating opacity above the Spanish SL.

Root cause: Politically exposed person (PEP) status of an ultimate shareholder, or layered offshore holding creating opacity above the Spanish SL.

Defense evidence: PEP screening declaration with passport copies, twelve-month bank statements evidencing the source of wealth, the official UBO register extract or notarized UBO attestation, and a sworn statement that no public funds, state-linked entities or third-party nominee accounts are used to finance the construction company.
Initial inbound capital injection routed through multiple intermediary banks in a non-EEA corridor, triggering source-of-funds scrutiny.

Root cause: Initial inbound capital injection routed through multiple intermediary banks in a non-EEA corridor, triggering source-of-funds scrutiny.

Defense evidence: Full SWIFT MT103 chain, the signed ISIC 4100 grain-silo-elevator construction contract or investment commitment letter, commercial registration extract of the foreign counterparty, certified translation of the project agreements, and a board resolution authorizing the exact contribution amount and account destination.

Cross-Border Clearing Corridors & Settlement Fit

Share capital must be wired before or simultaneously with notarization into the escrowed capital account opened in the name of the SL in formation. Where the entity adopts the progressive-formation (SLFS) modality under the Ley Crea y Crece, the initial subscribed amount may be below the €3,000 default statutory floor, but every subsequent capital increase must follow the same notarial deposit-certificate protocol. Routing in EUR uses SEPA Instant/TARGET2; routing in USD or third-country currency uses SWIFT MT103, with the remittance-information field carrying the purpose code mapped to 'Direct investment – incorporation and capital increase' and the beneficiary account exactly mirroring the notarial deed. Simultaneously, the transaction must be declared to the Banco de España BOPS portal and, if the foreign investor is non-EU/EFTA, screened against Law 19/2023 prior-authorization triggers. The Notary issues the deposit certificate only upon receipt of the bank's verifiable confirmation, after which the Registro Mercantil inscription proceeds.Domestic disbursements run over SEPA Credit Transfer (IBAN-based, same-day via TARGET2) and, for recurring subcontractor and material bills, SEPA Direct Debit. Cross-border trade settlements to non-EEA equipment vendors (slip-form rails, aeration towers, grain-handling steel) are executed by SWIFT MT103 against proof-of-shipment documents, or through irrevocable commercial Letters of Credit (UCP 600) advised via SWIFT MT700 and paid by MT103/MT202 upon presentation of compliant documents (commercial invoice, bill of lading, packing list, inspection certificate). Performance and advance-payment risks to the EPC client are covered by standby letters of credit (ISP98) or bank guarantees (U-form) issued by the onboarding tier-1 bank against the project's escrow and milestone milestones, preserving the low-risk AML classification of the construction flows.EUR/USD deliverable outright forwards traded bilaterally with the onboarding tier-1 bank under the ISDA 2002 Master Agreement and a Credit Support Annex.Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in EUR/BRL, EUR/MXN and other Latin American currencies to hedge expected USD- or local-currency receipts from export bridge contracts.Cross-currency swaps fixed-floating and fixed-fixed, permitted for longer-dated EUR/USD or EUR/other exposure arising from shareholder subordinated loans and capex financing.Vanilla FX options, collars and zero-premium structures under MiFID II suitability rules, approved through the entity's EII (professional client) classification.Spot-FX forwards and short-term FX swaps for working-capital roll-over of import LCs; all OTC derivative contracts are subject to EMIR reporting, bilateral margin where thresholds are exceeded, and intra-group hedging documentation where the parent treasury centralizes risk.

E-commerce / gateway settlement fit: Low-Medium feasibility: only European Economic Area (EEA) Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) validly passported into Spain under Law 21/2011 and PSD2 may lawfully serve as payment-account or e-money processors; they can expedite SEPA concentration and supplier disbursements but are not acceptors of statutory share-capital deposits because Spanish Notaries require a deposit certificate from a credit institution (bank) to authenticate the capital desembolso. Offshore, non-EEA EMIs have no legal mandate in Spain, cannot provide the notarial escrow evidence, and their use as treasury rail exposes the SL to adverse AML classification under Law 10/2010; therefore they should be confined to ancillary collection gateways only after a tier-1 bank account is live.

Stage 06

Corporate Tax & Transfer Pricing

Corporate income tax (CIT), box-by-box return breakdown, dividend WHT, and director personal liability.

Statutory corporate income tax (CIT)

25% general corporate income tax rate under Spanish Corporate Income Tax Law. Newly incorporated companies may generally apply a 15% rate during the first profitable tax period and the immediately following period, subject to statutory exclusions and anti-abuse conditions.

Dividend withholding tax (WHT)

19% Spanish withholding tax on dividends and other profit distributions to non-residents, subject to domestic exemptions and applicable tax treaties. A qualifying EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption may apply to a corporate EU or qualifying EEA parent generally holding at least 10% for the required continuous period, subject to taxation, anti-abuse, and beneficial-ownership conditions.

Mandatory Return Breakdown

Deadline: · Frequency:

The return is generally due within the first 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the end of the tax period. For a calendar-year taxpayer, the normal filing period is 1 to 25 July of the following year. Electronic filing deadlines may be extended to the next business day where legally applicable.

Deadline: · Frequency:

Modelo 216 is generally due within the first 20 calendar days of the month following the relevant month or quarter. Modelo 296 is generally due during the first 20 calendar days of January following the reporting year, subject to the applicable electronic filing calendar.

Transfer Pricing & Economic Substance

Master / Local File threshold: EUR 250,000 aggregate annual transaction value with the same related person, calculated at arm's-length value, is the principal threshold below which the detailed local documentation exemption may apply for transactions of the same type and under the same valuation method. The exemption generally does not cover certain real estate, intangible-asset, or tax-haven transactions. A Spanish entity belonging to a multinational group may require a Master File, and groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million may require Country-by-Country reporting. There is no single universal Master File threshold applicable to every group.

Economic substance scope: Spain does not operate a separate UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations filing regime. Nevertheless, Spanish anti-abuse rules, the beneficial-ownership requirement, the principal-purpose test, controlled foreign company rules, interest limitation rules, hybrid mismatch rules, general anti-avoidance provisions, and EU anti-abuse standards require genuine commercial substance. The SL should maintain Spanish management and decision-making evidence, qualified personnel or outsourced operational capacity, premises or operational infrastructure appropriate to its construction activity, project records, risk control, financing rationale, and contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation.

Fatal Compliance Red Lines & Director Liability

Tax evasion and fraudulent tax reporting

Statutory sanction: Administrative penalties may generally range from 50% to 150% of the unpaid tax, together with tax assessment, interest, and collection measures. Tax fraud exceeding EUR 120,000 per tax and tax period may constitute a criminal offense, generally punishable by imprisonment of 1 to 5 years and a fine of 1 to 6 times the amount defrauded. Aggravated cases may carry imprisonment of 2 to 6 years and higher fines.

Director personal liability: Directors or de facto managers who participate in, authorize, or negligently facilitate the conduct may face criminal liability, civil restitution, personal administrative liability in qualifying cases, disqualification from public office or management, and asset-securing measures. Travel restrictions are not automatic and require statutory or judicial grounds.
False invoicing and VAT carousel arrangements

Statutory sanction: Repayment of improperly claimed VAT and corporate deductions, late-payment interest, and administrative penalties commonly calculated by reference to the unpaid or unduly refunded tax. Serious or organized fraud may trigger criminal tax, commercial-document, or accounting offenses.

Director personal liability: Individuals who knowingly approve or use fictitious invoices may incur criminal and civil liability. Directors may be liable for losses caused by breach of diligence duties and may face asset measures, disqualification, or imprisonment where the conduct satisfies a criminal offense.
Transfer-pricing non-compliance

Statutory sanction: AEAT may make a primary adjustment and corresponding adjustments, assess tax and interest, and impose documentation-related penalties. Specific documentation penalties may apply per omitted, inaccurate, or incomplete data, subject to statutory caps; broader tax underpayment penalties may apply where tax is concealed or fraudulently avoided.

Director personal liability: Directors may face civil liability for approving materially unsupported related-party arrangements. Criminal exposure normally requires additional fraudulent conduct meeting the statutory elements of a tax, accounting, or commercial offense.
Improper treaty or EU directive relief

Statutory sanction: The SL may be assessed for withholding tax, interest, and penalties. Anti-abuse rules may deny treaty or directive relief and recharacterize the payment or arrangement according to its economic substance.

Director personal liability: Directors who knowingly provide false information or approve abusive withholding positions may face civil liability, administrative sanctions, and criminal liability where fraud, document falsification, or tax evasion thresholds are met.
Shell company and lack of economic substance

Statutory sanction: AEAT may apply recharacterization, conflict-in-application or simulation doctrines, deny deductions and treaty benefits, assess tax and interest, and impose penalties where applicable. Related-party payments may be reclassified as dividends or hidden profit distributions.

Director personal liability: Directors may incur civil liability and, in abusive or fraudulent cases, criminal liability. Corporate separateness is not automatically disregarded; veil piercing generally requires abuse of legal personality, fraud, insolvency abuse, or unlawful harm to creditors.
Withholding, payroll, and social-security non-compliance

Statutory sanction: The company may owe unpaid withholding, payroll tax, social-security contributions, interest, surcharges, and administrative penalties. Serious labor or social-security fraud may trigger criminal liability, particularly where workers' rights or public funds are materially affected.

Director personal liability: Directors may be jointly or subsidiarily liable in legally defined circumstances, particularly following non-compliance, insolvency, or failure to take corrective action. Criminal liability may include fines or imprisonment depending on the offense.
Anti-money laundering and terrorist-financing controls

Statutory sanction: Under Spanish AML legislation, serious and very serious breaches may lead to public or private reprimands, fines that can reach the higher of statutory fixed amounts, EUR 10 million, or 10% of annual total turnover for certain very serious breaches, together with management disqualification in applicable cases.

Director personal liability: Managers and officers responsible for AML failures may face personal administrative sanctions, civil liability, and criminal liability for money laundering or terrorist-financing participation. Travel bans are not automatic and require a competent-authority or judicial measure.
Construction-sector licensing, safety, and subcontracting violations

Statutory sanction: Labor, occupational-safety, construction, and sector regulators may impose fines, work stoppages, loss of eligibility for public contracts, contractor disqualification, and civil liability for accidents. Fatal or serious workplace incidents may result in criminal prosecution.

Director personal liability: Directors and site managers may face civil restitution, administrative sanctions, professional disqualification, and imprisonment for deliberate or grossly negligent conduct causing injury, death, or serious worker-rights violations.
Accounting, corporate-governance, and insolvency misconduct

Statutory sanction: Consequences may include rejection of accounts, tax reassessment, director liability for insolvency deficits, clawback of unlawful distributions, creditor claims, insolvency disqualification, and criminal penalties for accounting or insolvency offenses.

Director personal liability: Directors may be ordered to restore assets, compensate creditors, return unlawful distributions, or cover all or part of the insolvency shortfall. Imprisonment is possible where the conduct constitutes a criminal offense; travel restrictions require judicial authorization and are not automatic.
Sanctions, export-control, and prohibited-party exposure

Statutory sanction: Transactions may be blocked or confiscated and may attract administrative fines, loss of licenses, contracting restrictions, and criminal penalties under applicable Spanish, European Union, and international sanctions regimes.

Director personal liability: Directors and compliance officers who knowingly authorize prohibited transactions may face personal civil, administrative, and criminal liability. Asset freezes, investigative measures, and judicial travel restrictions may apply where legally ordered.
